column3: “Something” supplies an object for the command “eat.”
The Greek says the fields are “white,” rendered as “ripe,” and places “already” with this clause rather than the next verse.
In the Greek, “already” belongs to the preceding verse.
“Hard” and “now” are not separately present in the Greek.
The Greek says “no longer because of your speech,” rather than “not only because of your words.”
“Great” is not a separate modifier of the things He did; BSB leaves Galilee implicit at the start.
The Greek says “your son lives” in the present, rather than future “will live.”
The Greek describes him going down, rather than only being on the way.
The Greek asks when he “got better,” rather than specifically when he “had recovered.”
The Greek repeats the present “your son lives,” rather than future “will live.”
